source.title: Transfer entropy and O-information to detect grokking in tensor network multi-class classification problems
source.authors: Domenico Pomarico; Roberto Cilli; Alfonso Monaco; Loredana Bellantuono; Marianna La Rocca; Tommaso Maggipinto; Giuseppe Magnifico; Marlis Ontivero Ortega; Ester Pantaleo; Sabina Tangaro; Sebastiano Stramaglia; Roberto Bellotti; Nicola Amoroso

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; some encoding artifacts are present, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Applies training-dynamics and generalization analysis to three-class MPS classifiers on Fashion MNIST and hyperspectral imagery; it does not test the specific interventions or measurements in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports natural-label train/test performance and analyzes training dynamics. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size choices, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or example removal.
record.test_reason: The study measures natural-label accuracy and training dynamics of MPS classifiers, but none of its results tests V1–V8. Generalization and grokking in this setting do not establish random-label memorization capacity, effects of width or training choices, architectural comparisons, magnitude-aware sharpness, or effects of removing memorized examples.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors interpret the Fashion MNIST transition as grokking-like, accompanied by improved test accuracy, entanglement compression, output redundancy, and directional information flow. They describe the hyperspectral model as overfit, with persistent output synergy and weak directional information flow.
record.recipe_differences: MPS quantum-mask classifiers trained with two-site gradient descent on three-class, downsampled Fashion MNIST and PRISMA data; no random-label experiment or recipe matching the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and class: Fashion MNIST classes differ markedly in performance, and hyperspectral class accuracies also vary.

fits_no_version.finding: Fashion MNIST performance varies strongly by class: sneaker test accuracy is around 90%, while bag training accuracy is around 25% and test accuracy is below 10%; overall training accuracy saturates near 70%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: This three-class MPS classifier generalizes unevenly across classes on downsampled Fashion MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: PRISMA grapevine training/test accuracies are approximately 90%/50%, olive-tree accuracies almost 80%/35%, and cropland test accuracy approximately 28%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: This MPS classifier exhibits substantial train–test gaps on PRISMA land-cover classification.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors associate the Fashion MNIST accuracy transition with entanglement compression, positive output O-information, and directional transfer entropy; PRISMA output O-information remains negative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information-theoretic and entanglement diagnostics distinguish the learning dynamics of these two MPS classification tasks.

record.problems: The supplied results give no numerical overall test accuracy for Fashion MNIST and no stated chance baseline. The described class accuracies are approximate, and uncertainty is not provided for these values. The paper does not test arbitrary-label memorization or the specific interventions and measures in V1–V8.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible train/test accuracy results are stated numerically in the text; overall values shown in Figure 3 are not described with numbers in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label training, near-perfect random-label fit, or matched natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold; discussing controllable MPS bond dimension does not test this effect.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or test of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison or comparison of tuning regimes.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
No dropout intervention or comparison involving dropout, weight decay, and augmentation.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, sharpness–gap ranking, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures. Entanglement entropy and information measures are different constructs.
No inclusion-based memorization estimates or retraining after removing memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification to discusses/T6. Numerical row values agree with the supplied text. The authors' grokking interpretation does not supply the random-label experiment required by V1, and their proposed generalization diagnostics do not measure the sharpness construct in V7.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of random-label and natural-label generalization.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with other generalization measures.
